No tests. Dist is built; we should build at end. Now design details & implement. ### UX flow 1. Player says phrase → `game.forgeWeapon(phrase)`: - If not playing → return null (existing behavior probably). - If phrase empty → return. - Create weapon object and store as pending: `this.harvest = { phrase, weapon, words, blocksTotal, collected, groups: [...] }`. - Clear previous collectibles and their meshes. - Spawn one cluster per word around the arena. Each cluster: 10 small cubes arranged in a ring/grid, plus word label sprite floating above, plus thin beacon. - Notify `callbacks.onHarvestStart?.(state)`. - Return weapon object (so callers can use `weapon.kind`), but maybe main should display "coletando" toast not "materializada". The `onForge` should only fire at completion. - Maybe restructure: `forgeWeapon(phrase)` returns recipe weapon immediately but does not setWeapon. It starts harvest. Callers in main still use returned kind in toast. But toast "“x” → CANHÃO DE..." is okay-ish though it's pending. Better update main to show collection toast and transcript accordingly. 2. During update when playing: - Animate blocks (bob, spin, label sprites). - Check distance to player; when < pickupRadius, collect: mark collected, remove block with burst/audio, increment count, callback `onHarvestProgress`. - Maybe magnet: if within 2.2, move toward player. - When count === total: call `completeHarvest()` → setWeapon(weapon, true), callbacks.onForge, onHarvestComplete, audio.materialize. The `setWeapon` calls `onWeapon` which shows "ARMA MATERIALIZADA". We can have collection HUD show completion then hide after 1.6s. Main callback can control. 3. If a new phrase while collecting: - `beginHarvest` cancels old, new recipe. It should notify and reset progress. Maybe not count previously collected toward new phrase. That's simplest and consistent. 4. If player dies or returns to menu or restarts: - clear collectibles and harvest state, hide HUD. 5. Pause: update returns before harvest update, so blocks freeze (fine). 6. Existing default weapon: At run start, player has "pistola de acesso". The mechanic applies only when forging a new weapon. ### Spawning positions Arena walkable region: radius 2.65 to 25.1, obstacles at 4 spots with radius ~1.7. Need avoid obstacles and center obelisk. For each word group i of N: - Choose anchor angle distributed evenly with random jitter: base = (i / N) * TAU + random offset (global random offset), radius = 12-22. - Ensure anchor distance from player start? Player moves. - Cluster of 10 blocks arranged in 2 rows x 5? To make it collectible in a pass, use a tight spiral/ring radius 0.7-1.2. Actually pickup radius 1.1; if all blocks within ~1.5 radius, walking to center collects all. That's satisfying and quick. But the "collect all little blocks" visually works: 10 cubes arranged in two concentric rings (5+5) with spacing 0.6, radius 0.6 and 1.15. Player walking through collects all. - y ~ 0.45-0.8 with bob. - Cluster anchor label above y=2.2 showing word. - Beacon: thin cylinder from y=0 to 4, transparent element color, additive, low opacity. Could be visually noisy with 12 words. Maybe only beacon column faint (opacity 0.08) and label. It helps find. - Maybe use a ring on the floor at anchor. If 120 blocks (12 words), 12 clusters around arena is fine. Word labels: `makeTextTexture(word.toUpperCase(), '10 BLOQUINHOS')` sprite. But makeTextTexture uses fixed 74px; long words may overflow. Could create a new helper for labels with dynamic width and font. Or use a canvas 512 with `ctx.font` size computed based on word length. Let's write `makeWordLabelTexture(word)` with canvas 512x128, background transparent, text centered, font size min(64, 430 / (word.length*0.55)) with display font. Use color acid/cyan. Sprite scale based on texture aspect (4:1), e.g. width 2.4, height 0.6. It faces camera automatically (THREE.Sprite). Position anchor y=2.0. Add to scene as part of group. Important: Sprite material transparent, depthWrite false, maybe depthTest true so hidden behind walls but visible within arena. Good. Could add scale pulse. Cluster label should be above blocks, and word counter? Maybe show word index? Not needed. ### Performance Up to 120 cubes. Each as separate Mesh = 120 draw calls. Could use InstancedMesh per material? Different groups, all same material? We can create one InstancedMesh per element color? Simpler: use shared geometry/material across all blocks, and individual meshes (120 draw calls) is okay. But Three.js scene has lots already. Fine for modern. Could optimize with InstancedMesh but pickup removal requires per-instance visibility; we can set matrices to zero scale. But then animation per-instance each frame. It's manageable but complex. Individual meshes with shared geometry/material is straightforward; disposal careful not to dispose shared geometry/material multiple times. `disposeMesh` traverses and disposes. If shared, disposing one block would break others. So create per-block geometry/material? 120 small BoxGeometry and materials is okay memory-wise; but avoid shared disposal issue. Could create one geometry and clone materials? Or per-block geometry. Fine. Actually simpler: each block gets its own BoxGeometry and MeshStandardMaterial? 120 materials expensive. Use one shared geometry and one shared material per harvest; on cleanup, remove meshes then dispose shared geometry/material once. Implement custom cleanup instead of `disposeMesh`. Track `this.harvestResources = { geometry, materials: [], labels }`. Or use `THREE.InstancedMesh` for blocks: single draw call, animate via matrix updates each frame. Let's evaluate effort. InstancedMesh count = total blocks; per block data includes position, phase, scale, collected. Update matrices each frame for floating/spin. Matrix compose from quaternion/scale. Up to 120 * per frame trivial. For magnet, update positions. Collection: set matrix to zero scale. Need raycast not used. This is clean and performant. But color per cluster (words all same element color, so one material works). Use `MeshStandardMaterial` emissive color. Add a second InstancedMesh for glow? Skip; use emissive and a point of additive sprite per cluster maybe. However instanced meshes + per-instance color if we want each word cluster same color - fine single color. But the user said map made of mini blocks. Blocks could be styled as little neon cubes. We can use BoxGeometry(0.28, 0.28, 0.28) with slight bevel? Box is fine. Each block rotates individually, floats. For instanced, compose matrix with rotation. Good. Implement: ``` spawnHarvest(phrase) { this.clearHarvest(); const words = splitWords(phrase); const weapon = createWeaponFromPhrase(phrase); // but title might trim; words should be from the phrase we pass ... } ``` Wait weapon phrase is titleFor(raw) and may truncate >72; words for recipe should be from the same sanitized phrase. Use `weapon.phrase`. Word count should be words in `weapon.phrase`. But "each word" includes stopwords. Yes. Cap: `MAX_BLOCKS = 120`, `MAX_WORDS = 12`. If >12 words, maybe use first 12 for clusters? But weapon phrase may be 72 chars ~ 12 words max. Input maxlength 72. Voice could be longer, but titleFor truncates at 72 with ellipsis. 13 words possible with short words. We can allow up to 12 clusters and distribute blocks? Hmm. Requirement each word 10. Better `words = all words`, `total = words.length * 10` no cap but 72 chars limits to maybe 15 words (e.g. "a a a..." 24 words). Collecting 240 blocks is awful. Put cap at 12 words: for words beyond 12, they still count as words? Then 10 blocks each won't be visible? Could group overflow blocks into existing clusters. Simpler: `const words = splitWords(weapon.phrase).slice(0, 12)` and note? Not faithful. Maybe no cap but 72 max chars = with single-letter words max ~36 words = 360 blocks.
